RAJYA SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2765 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22.12.2021 
 
Adoption of private publishers' books instead of NCERT by private schools 
 
2765 Shri Vijay Pal Singh Tomar: 
 
Will the Minister of Education be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government is aware of the fact that most of the private schools force 
their students to read books published by some private publishers instead of 
NCERT; 
 
(b) whether NCERT books are very valuable for making careers of the students 
as well as for preparing for competitive examinations, but some private 
schools are not adopting these books; and 
 
(c) if so, whether any action/instructions have been taken/issued by Gover nment 
to these private schools to use the NCERT books in their schools particularly 
in primary and secondary schools? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF EDUCATION 
)SMT. ANNPURNA DEVI) 
 
(a) to (c): In view of plurality of textbooks advocated in National Curriculum 
Framework 2005, the affiliation bylaws of Central Board of Secondary Education 
(CBSE) stipulate that school may prescribe National Council of Educational 
Research and Training ( NCERT) textbooks in the classes and subjects in which 
these have been published by the NCERT.  Extreme care should be taken in the 
selection of books of private publishers so that there is no objectionable content that 
hurts the feeling of any class, community, gender, or religious group in society. 
 
The school shall also put a list of prescribed books on its website with the 
written declaration duly signed by the Manager and the Principal to the effect that 
they have gone through the contents of the books prescr ibed by the school and own 
the responsibility. If a school is found prescribing a book having any objectionable 
content, the responsibility for such content shall be with the school and action will be 
initiated against the school by the Board. 
 
CBSE syllabus for classes IX to XII recommends NCERT textbooks wherever 
available and CBSE has also issued a detailed circular No. 04/2013 dated 14 th May, 
2013 regarding textbooks for classes’ I-VIII in May, 2013.  CBSE issues advisories to 
schools from time to time about not to force parents to buy additional textbooks and 
follow the guidelines laid down by the Board in this regard  vide Circular No (s). 
Acad.41/2015 dated July 20,  2015; Acad.13/2016 dated April 12,  2016; and 
Circular(Aff).08/2018 dated June 21,  2018.  These circulars are also available on 
CBSE website: www.cbse.nic.in

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ PAUSHA 1, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
INCREASE IN UNREST IN JAMMU & KASHMIR 
 
2770.      SHRI MALLIKARJUN KHARGE: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:  
 
(a) the reasons why there has been a sudden increase in unrest and 
targeted attacks on religious minorities in the UT of Jammu & Kashmir; 
 
(b) the reasons why the UT administration has failed to control the 
proliferation of such incidents; 
 
(c) how many arrests have been made in connection with these incidents; 
(d) how many have been chargesheeted; and 
 
(e) whether the creation of a new anti-terror agency in the UT signals the 
failure of existing agencies in tackling the situation and if so, the reason 
therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b): There has been an overall decline in terrorist incidents from 417 
in 2018 to 203 in 2021 (till 30 th November, 2021) and the law and order 
situation in Jammu & Kashmir has improved. However, there have been a 
few targeted attacks on people belonging to religious minority communities 
by terrorists sponsored from across the border. A robust security and 
intelligence  grid  is in place to prevent any terrorist attack.  In addition, day 
 
 
128

 
-2- 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2770 FOR 22.12.2021 
 
& night area domination, patrolling and proactive operations against 
terrorists are being carried out.  Besides, round the clock checking at 
Nakas, Road Opening Parties are being adequately augmented at strategic 
points to thwart any terrorist attack. 
 
(c): 07 persons have been arrested in connection with attacks on religious 
minorities while 04 terrorists involved in these incidents have been killed. 
 
(d): 07 accused including 01 absconder have been charge sheeted. 
 
(e): No Sir.  The State Investigation Agency (SIA) has been constituted by 
the Govt. of Jammu and Kashmir for speedy and effective investigation and 
prosecution of terrorism related cases.  Moreover, SIA shall be the nodal 
agency for coordinating with the National Investigation Agency (NIA) and 
other Central Agencies in this regard.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-2773 
ANSWERED ON-22/12/2021 
  
UNREGISTERED VEHICLES IN INDIA 
 
2773.     SHRI SANJAY SINGH: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:- 
  
(a) whether Government plans to analyze the extent of unregistered vehicles in India; 
(b) if so, the details thereof along with methodology used to measure the number of unregistered 
vehicles in India; 
(c) whether a clampdown of such vehicles would possibly impact the safety of our roads; and 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (d) Section 39 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 mandates that no person shall drive 
any motor vehicle and no owner of a motor vehicle shall cause or permit the vehicle to be 
driven in any public place or in any other place unless the vehicle is registered in accordance 
with Chapter IV of the Act and the certificate of registration o f the vehicle has not been 
suspended or cancelled and the vehicle caries a registration mark displayed in the prescribed 
manner. Implementation of provisions of Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989 and Motor 
Vehicles Act, 1988 comes under the purview of the State/UT government.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2776 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ PAUSHA 01, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
PROMOTION OF INSPECTOR (STENOGRAPHER) 
 
2776.  SHRI B. LINGAIAH YADAV: 
 
Will the Minister of Home Affairs be pleased to refer to answer to Unstarred 
Question 2597 given in the Rajya Sabha on 11th August, 2021 and to state: 
 
(a) the manner/mechanism through which confirmed Inspector 
(Stenographer) shall be promoted to next rank in case there is no 
sanctioned post of ACP (Stenographer) and no need to create separate 
posts as replied; 
 
(b) whether services of confirmed Inspector (Stenographer) with 30 years of 
service, may be utilized as ACP/HQ/Admin in view of similar job profile; and 
 
(c) the current status of the proposal, the reasons for no initiative in the 
matter since 2012, and whether any action has been taken by Ministry in 
this regard? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a): Delhi Police (Promotion and Confirmation) Amendment Rules specify the 
mechanism for promotional avenues of persons appointed as Stenographers 
in Delhi Police. The initial appointment in the stenographer cadre is as 
Assistant Sub-Inspector (Stenographer), and thereafter, promotional 
avenues are available for an Assistant Sub-Inspector (Stenographer) for 
elevation as Sub-Inspector (Stenographer) and Inspector (Stenographer).  
As per Rule 17(iv) of the aforesaid Rules, an Inspector (Stenographer) is not  
 
145

 
-2- 
 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2776 FOR 22.12.2021 
eligible for inclusion in the Common Seniority List of Inspectors being 
considered for induction into DANIPS. Promotion of the eligible elevated 
Sub-Inspector (Stenographer) shall be subject to furnishing of an 
undertaking from the existing Sub-Inspector/Assistant Sub-Inspector 
(Stenographer), that he/she is aware that he/she has no claim to get 
inducted in DANIPS Cadre. Delhi Police personnel in Stenographer cadre are 
granted Modified Assured Career Progression (MACP) after attaining 10, 20 
and 30 years of service in levels 7, 8 and 9 respectively, as per guidelines of 
Department of Personnel and Training (DoPT). 
(b): As reported by Delhi Police, at present there is no post of ACP/HQ 
(Admn.) available in Delhi Police. As such the question for utilization of 
service of Inspector (Stenographer) against the said post does not arise.  
(c): No proposal has been received by Ministry of Home Affairs on this issue.

LOSS DUE TO NATURAL DISASTERS 
 
2779.  SHRI MD. NADIMUL HAQUE: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:   
(a) the annual economic loss incurred from various extreme weather events 
in the country during the last five years, the State-wise details thereof; 
 
(b) whether the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA) or any 
State Disaster Management Authorities (SDMAs) use financial tools like 
catastrophe risk financing, risk insurance, micro-insurance, etc. to 
compensate for massive losses on account of disasters; 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not, the reasons therefor; and 
 
(d) the financial assistance given by Government to different States as 
against the economic losses suffered by the States due to disasters during 
the last five years? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a):  This Ministry does not maintain centralized data about economic loss 
incurred from various extreme weather events in the country.  However, 
State-wise details of human lives lost, houses/ huts damaged and crop area 
affected due to hydro-meteorological calamities, during the last five years, 
i.e. 2016-17 to 2020-21, as assessed/ reported by the State Governments/ 
Union Territories, are at Annexure-I.   
 
 
 
156

 
-2-

(b) and (c):   National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), under the 
National Cyclone Risk Management Project (NCRMP), has appointed a 
Consulting firm to carry out Comprehensive Multi-hazard Risk Financing 
Strategy covering four States (Gujarat, Kerala, Odisha & Uttarakhand) for 
development of disaster risk financing strategy and identification of risk 
transfer instruments for them.  The scheduled completion date of this 
consulting contract is 15th July, 2022.  
(d): The primary responsibility for disaster management rests with the 
State Governments concerned. The State Governments undertake relief 
measures in the wake of natural disasters from the State Disaster 
Response Fund (SDRF), already placed at their disposal, in accordance with 
Government of India’s approved items and norms.  Additional financial 
assistance is provided from National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF), as 
per laid down procedure in case of disaster of ‘severe nature’, which 
includes an assessment based on the visit of an Inter-Ministerial Central 
Team (IMCT).   
State-wise details of allocation and releases from SDRF/ State Disaster Risk 
Management Fund (SDRMF) [after recommendations of 15 th Finance 
Commission, which includes SDRF and State Disaster Mitigation Fund 
(SDMF)] and NDRF during the last five years, i.e., 2016-17 to 2020-21 are

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2780 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ PAUSHA 01, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
EMPLOYMENT OPPORTUNITIES IN THE NAXALITE AFFECTED AREAS OF 
ODISHA 
 
2780.  SHRI SUJEET KUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:   
(a) whether any steps have been taken by Government to create 
employment opportunities in the Naxalite affected areas of Odisha to 
prevent unemployed people to join Naxal groups; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether Government will consider sanctioning additional funds to the 
aspirational districts of Odisha to impart skill development and job 
opportunities to the youths; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a& b): The National Policy Action Plan to address Left Wing Extremism 
(LWE), approved in 2015,  has development as one of the most important 
component. Apart from flagship schemes of the line Ministries of 
Government of India, several specific development schemes have been 
implemented in LWE affected areas including Odisha to improve road and 
telecom connectivity, financial inclusion, skill development, education etc.  
 
160

-2- 
 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2780 FOR 22.12.2021 
Employment at the local level is generated with implementation of all such 
schemes and as a consequence of resultant economic growth.  
 
More than 9600 km roads have already been constructed in LWE affected 
areas under the specific schemes line Road Requirement Plan-I (RRP -I) and 
Road Connectivity project for LWE affected areas (RCPLWEA) . 2343 mobile 
towers were installed under Phase-I and 2542 towers approved under 
phase-II of Mobile Connectivity Project for LWE Affected Areas . Rs. 2698 
crore has be en released since 2017 to „Most LWE Affected Districts‟ under 
the scheme „Special Central Assistance (SCA)‟ to fill the critical gaps in 
public infrastructure and services. 
 
Special focus has been given to Skill Development and Entrepreneurship of 
the youth in these areas. 47 Industrial Training Institutes (ITI) and 68 Skill 
Development Centres (SDC) have been approved under “Skill Development 
Scheme in 47 Districts affected by LWE” with an estimated cost of Rs. 
407.85 crore. Of these, 06 ITIs and 10 SDCs have been approved in 06 LWE 
affected districts of Odisha. Further, 5,36,427 candidates have been trained 
in the State of Odisha till date under the flagship scheme Pradhan Mantri 
Kaushal Vikas Yojana  (PMKVY).  
 
 
161

-3- 
 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2780 FOR 22.12.2021 
(c) & (d): The main strategy of the „Aspirational Districts Programme‟ is 
bringing convergence of existing schemes which have their own funding 
arrangements. Therefore, large infusion of additional funds is not envisaged 
under this programme.  
 
However, to foster competitive spirit and address critical gaps, a provision 
of additional allocation is there for districts securing good ranks based on 
their monthly incremental progress. The first and second rankers in overall 
terms are awarded Rs. 10 crore and Rs. 5 crore respectively. The first 
ranker from each of the five sectors is awarded Rs. 3 crore each. As per 
this method, the Aspirational Districts of Gajapati, Nuapada, Bolangir, 
Malkangiri, Nabarangpur, Dhenkanal, Kalahandi, Kandhamal and Koraput in 
Odisha, have been sanctioned a cumulative amount of approximately Rs. 
43.30 crores for projects formulated by the Districts in sectors line 
including Health & Nutrition, Education, Agriculture & Water Resources and 
Financial Inclusion & Skill Development

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO -2781 
ANSWERED ON – 22/12/2021 
 
PROPOSAL TO MAKE NHS TOLL FREE 
 
2781. SHRI A. VIJAYAKUMAR: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of the longest and shortest National Highway in the country; 
(b) whether there is any proposal to make all National Highways toll free; and 
(c) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) The longest National Highway (NH) in the country is NH-27 (East – West Corridor) , 
having length of about 4,113 km, while the shortest NH is NH-327B in the State of West Bengal 
having length of about 1.20 km. 
(b) and (c) There is no such proposal to make all National Highways toll free.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2782 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ PAUSHA 01, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
INCREASE IN WOMEN REPRESENTATION IN THE POLICE FORCE 
 
2782.  SHRI BHASKAR RAO NEKKANTI: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:   
(a) the details of the visits by 5 advisories who were asked to go to all 
States from 22 nd June, 2021 in order to increase women representation in 
the police force to 33 percent; 
 
(b) whether State Governments have accepted the request to create 
additional posts of women constables and SIs by converting the vacant 
posts of male constables; and 
 
(c) if so, the details thereof and, if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (c) “Police” is a State subject falling in List -II (State List) of the 
Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India. It is primarily the 
responsibility of the State Governments/UT Administrations to recruit police 
personnel including improvement of gender bal ance in police force. This 
Ministry has not sent any advisor to visit States on the subject however, 
Ministry has issued advisories to the States for increasing number of 
women in the police forces. The Ministry of Home Affairs has issued 
advisories dated 22.04.2013, 21.05.2014, 12.05.2015,   21.06.2019 and 
22.06.2021 to all  the State  Governments to increase the representation of  
164

-2- 
R.S. US.Q.NO. 2782 FOR 22.12.2021 
women police to 33% of the total strength. All the State Governments have 
been requested to create additional posts of women Constables/Sub-
Inspectors by converting the vacant posts of male constables. The aim is 
that each police station should have at least 3 women Sub-Inspectors and 
10 women police Constables, so that a women help desk is manned round 
the clock. 
States have also been advised to strengthen welfare measures for women 
police personnel such as provision of housing, medical facilities and 
conducive work environment.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2783 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ PAUSHA 01, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
LOSS OF LIVES AND PROPERTIES DUE TO FLOODS AND CYCLONES 
 
2783.  SHRI ANAND SHARMA: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:   
(a) whether loss of lives, properties and livelihood have taken place due to 
frequent floods and cyclones in the country during the last three years; 
 
(b) whether standard protocols to mitigate such disasters exist; 
 
(c) whether mitigating measures are taken by Government, if so, the State-
wise details thereof; and 
 
(d) if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS 
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
(a) to (d):  This Ministry does not maintain the centralized data about loss of 
lives, properties & livelihood due to natural disasters including floods & 
cyclones.  However, State-wise details of the human lives lost, house/huts 
damaged and crops area affected due to hydro-meteorological calamities, 
during the last three years, i.e., 2018-19, 2019-2020 and 2020-2021, as 
assessed/reported by the State Governments / Union Territories, are at 
Annexure. 
 
 
166

-2- 
 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2783 FOR 22.12.2021 
There are institutional mechanisms, at the National and the State levels, for 
effective management of natural disasters.  The primary responsibility for 
disaster management, including taking mitigating measures, rests with the 
State Government concerned.  The Disaster Management Act, 2005, 
provides for the integration of measures for the prevention of disasters and 
mitigation into the development plans and projects, in accordance with the 
guidelines of the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA).  
The Central Government has established a robust early warning system and 
has significantly enhanced the accuracy of weather forecasts. Forecasting 
agencies are continuing their efforts for the improvement of warning and 
dissemination systems vigorously.  Mock exercises and community 
awareness programmes are being regularly conducted to educate 
people/farmers at the time of natural calamities. 
Multi-purpose cyclone shelters and early warning systems created in the 
Coastal States under the National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) 
have proved to be of great help during recent cyclones.  The measures, 
taken by the Central and State Governments, have significantly improved 
the disaster management practices, preparedness, prevention, mitigation 
and response mechanisms resulting in significant reduction in casualties 
during  natural  calamities,  including  floods  and  cyclones,  in the country.   
167

-3- 
 
R.S.US.Q.NO.2783 FOR 22.12.2021 
Strengthening of the disaster management is a continuing and evolving 
process of governance.  
Further, the 15 th Finance Commission, in its report, has made a separate 
allocation of Rs. 13,693 crore for National Disaster Mitigation Fund (NDMF) 
and Rs. 32,031 crore for State Disaster Mitigation Fund (SDMF) for the 
award period of 2021-2026 for undertaking mitigation measures.

NRIs HARASSED AT AIRPORTS

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2788 
 
TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ 01 PAUSHA, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
CYCLONE RISK MITIGATION PROJECTS 
 
2788.  DR. KANIMOZHI NVN SOMU: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has left out Tamil Nadu from National Cyclone Risk 
Mitigation (NCRM) Projects phase-I and II which were implemented to respond 
better to cyclones and for the construction of infrastructure to address the 
vulnerability of coastal community to cyclones; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) the effective measures taken by Government to implement projects under 
NCRM in Tamil Nadu; and 
 
(d) the details of the funds allocated for the projects under NCRM? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) to (c): National Cyclone Risk Mitigation Project (NCRMP) is a World Bank 
assisted centrally sponsored scheme, being implemented in the 8 coastal States, 
in two phases.  Two States were covered in Phase-I, namely, Andhra Pradesh and 
Odisha; and six States are covered in Phase- II, namely Goa, Gujarat, Karnataka, 
Kerala, Maharashtra and West Bengal.  The project has the following four 
components: 
i. Component A: Early Warning Dissemination System (EWDS), the state of 
the art multi-technology option (Alert Siren, Satellite Radio, Mass 
Messaging, etc.), to provide reliable communication and ensuring last 
mile connectivity during disaster. 
-2/... 
178

-2- 
RS.US.Q.NO.2788 FOR 22.12.2021 
ii. Component B: Cyclone Risk Mitigation Infrastructure (CRMI), to enhance 
the preparedness and mitigate the vulnerability of the coastal 
communities through investments for construction of multi- purpose 
cyclone shelters (MPCS), roads, bridges and saline embankments. 
iii. Component C: Technical Assistance for Capacity Building on multi 
hazard risk management. 
iv. Component D: Project Management and Monitoring. 
 
At the time of the inception of NCRMP, as Tamil Nadu State was already 
implementing a similar World Bank assisted project, 
viz, “Coastal Disaster Risk 
Reduction Project” , with a total outlay of Rs. 1481.80 crore, having similar 
components, it was not made part of NCRMP. 
(d): Revised fund allocation under NCRMP Phase-I and NCRMP Phase- II are Rs. 
2541.60 crore and Rs. 2059.83 crore, respectively.

offences involving punishment for more than six years, if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY KUMAR MISHRA)

in States/Union Territories.

TO BE ANSWERED ON THE 22ND DECEMBER, 2021/ 01 PAUSHA, 1943 (SAKA) 
 
CLUBBING OF CASES UNDER POCSO ACT 
 
2791.  DR. AMAR PATNAIK: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government clubs reporting of cases from Section 17-22 under the 
Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act; 
 
(b) if so, the reasons therefor and if not, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether Government clubs reporting of cases under POCSO for Section 4 with 
Section 6 and Section 8 with Section 10; 
 
(d) if so, the reasons therefor and if not, the details thereof; and 
 
(e) whether Government is aware that study indicates the lack of invoking 
aggravated charges under the POCSO Act, if so, the steps taken to mitigate it? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI AJAY KUMAR MISHRA) 
 
(a) to (d) The National Crime Records Bureau (NCRB) collects and compiles crime 
statistics from States/ Union Territories as per defined protocol and format , 
including statistics on cases reported under the Prevention of Children from 
Sexual Offence (POCSO) Act , and publishes it in its annual publication ‘Crime in 
India’. The data may be grouped in this publication for statistical representation.  
(e) ‘Police’ and ‘Public order’ are State subjects as per the Seventh Schedule to 
the Constitution of India. The responsibility of maintaining law and order, 
protection of life and property of the citizens, rests with the respective State 
Governments. They are competent to deal with such offences under the extant 
provisions of laws.

PROTECTION OF VULNERABLE WITNESSES 
 
2792.  SHRI G.C. CHANDRASHEKHAR: 
 
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government has complied with the orders of the Supreme Court in 
the case of Mahender Chawla and Ors. Vs Union of India and Ors. to provide 
financial support to the States to establish Vulnerable Witness Deposition 
Complexes in the States; 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof including budgetary allocations and funds released 
and if not, the reasons therefor; 
 
(c) whether Government has tracked implementation of the Witness Protection 
Scheme 2018 across States; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof, including funds allocated and released toward the 
scheme and the list of implementing States, and if not, the reasons therefor? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS  
(SHRI NITYANAND RAI) 
 
(a) & (b): The primary responsibility of development of Infrastructure facilities in 
this regard rests with the State Governments. To augment the resources of the 
State Governments, the Union Government has been implementing a Centrally 
Sponsored Scheme for Development of Infrastructure Facilities in district and 
subordinate courts by providing financial assistance to State Governments / UTs 
in the prescribed fund sharing pattern.  
The Scheme is being implemented since 1993-94. Till date the Central 
Government has sanctioned Rs. 8709.77 crore under the Scheme to States/UTs. 
-2/... 
184

-2- 
RS.US.Q.NO.2792 FOR 22.12.2021 
The Government has extended the above scheme for a further period of five 
years from 01.04.2021 to 31.03.2026, with a total budgetary outlay of Rs.9000 
crores, including Central share of Rs.5307 crores.  
(c) & (d): The Hon’ble Supreme Court of India in its Judgment dated 05.12.2018 in 
Writ Petition (Criminal) No. 156 of 2016 has endorsed the Witness Protection 
Scheme, 2018.  
‘Police’ and ‘Public Order’ are State subjects under the Seventh Schedule to the 
Constitution of India and the States/UTs are responsible for implementation of 
the Scheme.  
The Scheme provides for a State Witness Protection Fund for meeting the 
expenses of the scheme. This fund shall be operated by the Department of Home 
under State/UT Government and shall comprise of the following:  
i. Budgetary allocation made in the Annual Budget by the State Government;  
ii. Receipt of amount of costs imposed/ ordered to be deposited by the 
courts/tribunals in the Witness Protection Fund;  
iii. Donations/ contributions from Philanthropist/ Charitable Institutions/ 
Organizations and individuals permitted by the Government.  
iv. Funds contributed under Corporate Social Responsibility.

-3-

The Ministry of Home Affairs has requested the State Governments/UT 
Administration vide its letter dated 14.01.2019 to implement the Witness 
Protection Scheme as per the direction of the Hon’ble Supreme Court. 
Subsequently, Ministry of Home Affairs from time to time has written to 
States/UTs for the implementation of the ‘Witness Protection Scheme, 2018’.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2793 
ANSWERED ON 22.12.2021 
 
DEVOLUTION OF POWER AND FUNDS TO PRIS 
 
2793 DR. FAUZIA KHAN: 
 
Will the Minister of Panchayati Raj be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government proposes to give more powers and funds to the Panchayati Raj 
Institutions (PRIs); 
 
(b) if so, the details thereof, along with the number of requests received from the State 
Governments including Maharashtra in this regard, State-wise; 
 
(c) whether the NITI Aayog h as made recommendations in this regard and any policy is 
being worked out to make PRIs successful; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof and the action taken by Government for effective 
implementation of the said policy? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) & (b) Article 243G of the Constitution of India empowers the Legislature of a State to make 
provisions, by law, for the devolution of power and responsibilities upon Panchayat at 
appropriate level, subject to such conditions, as may be, specified with respect to  the 
preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and implementation of 
schemes for economic development and social justice as may be entrusted to them including 
those in relation to matters included in the Eleventh Schedule.  The State legislatures are to 
consider the 29 subjects illustratively set out in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution to the 
Panchayats.  The performance of the Panchayats depends on the extent of powers and resources 
devolved to them, which varies from State to St ate. As ‘local government’, which includes 
Panchayats, is a State subject, Ministry of Panchayati Raj has been advocating to the States for 
increased devolution of powers to the Panchayats . Similarly, by successive Finance 
Commissions, more funds have been provided to the States for distribution among Panchayati 
Raj Institutions (PRIs) as under:- 
187

1. Tenth Finance Commission (1995-2000) : Rs. 4380.93 crore 
2. Eleventh Finance Commission(2000-2005) : Rs. 8000.00 crore 
3. Twelfth Finance Commission (2005-2010) : Rs. 20,000.00 crore 
4. Thirteenth Finance Commission (2010-15) : Rs. 63,050.00 crore 
5. Fourteenth Finance Commission(2015-2020) : Rs. 2,00,292.20 crore 
6. Fifteenth Finance Commission(2020-2026) : Rs. 2,97,555.00 crore 
 
As the  devolution of powers to Panchayats is within the purview  of States, no request is 
required to be made by them to the Government of India. Regarding allocation of funds, in this 
regard, Finance Commission, prior to making recommendations holds detailed discussion with 
stakeholders, including a ll States  and takes into consideration  their suggestions in its 
recommendations. 
 
(c) & (d) A Committee was constituted under the chairmanship of Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog 
for restructuring of Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan (RGSA) to address the challenges faced 
by the rural local bodies and increased fund flow to Gram Panchayats . Based on the 
recommendations of the Committee, a revamped Centrally Sponsored Scheme of RGSA was 
prepared for strengthening of PRIs for the period 2018-2019 to 2021-22.

INSTALLATION OF STREET LIGHTS IN GRAM PANCHAYATS OF TAMIL 
NADU 
 
2794. SHRI K.R.N. RAJESHKUMAR: 
 
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government provides funds to Gram Panchayats for street lighting in villages, 
if so, the details thereof during the last three years, State/UT -wise including Tamil 
Nadu; 
 
(b) whether Government has demanded utilisation certificate of funds from concerned 
authorities and if so, the details thereof; 
 
(c) whether any actual target for fund utilization has been fixed for the said purpose, if so, 
the details thereof and achievements made thereon, State/UT-wise including Tamil 
Nadu; 
 
(d) whether any time-frame has been fixed for providing street lights in all the villages in 
the country; and 
 
(e) if so, the details thereof?  
 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) Under the Fourteenth Finance Commission (XIV FC) award for the period of 2015 -2020, 
grants to the tune of Rs.2,00,292.20 crore were allocated to Gram Panchayats (GPs) in 26 States 
including Tamil Nadu. The Grant was provided to GPs for delivering basic services including 
street-lighting. Under Fifteenth Finance Commission (XV FC), Grants to the tune of Rs. 60,750 
crore are allocated for the interim period FY 2020 -21 and Rs.2,36,805 Crore are allocated for 
the period FY 2021 -26 to Panchayats in all the t hree tiers and Traditional Local Bodies and 
Sixth Schedule areas in 28 States  including Tamil Nadu. The Grants are in two parts namely 
Basic (Untied) Grants and Tied Grants. The Untied Grants can be utilised for felt needs on 29 
subjects enshrined under Schedule XI of the Constitution including street lighting. State -wise 
status of allocation and release of XIV FC Grants for the F.Y. 2018 -19 and 2019-20 and XV 
189

FC Grants for the F.Y. 2020-21 is given at Annexure. Under the Finance Commission Grants, 
funds are provided only to States and not to Union Territories. 
 
(b) Release of subsequent installments of the Grants under XIV FC and XV FC award is subject 
to submission of utilization certificate / grant transfer certificate for the previous installments 
drawn along with compliance of other stipulated conditions by the States.  
 
(c) to (e) No, Sir. The Panchayats incur expenditure on basic services as per their approved 
Panchayat Development Plan based on local felt needs and priorities.

PROGRESS UNDER SVAMITVA SCHEME 
  
2795. SMT. ROOPA GANGULY: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the number of land records that have been finalised under the SVAMITVA scheme, the 
State-wise details thereof;  
 
(b) the number of loans that has been taken by keeping these land records as collateral,  the 
details thereof;  
 
(c) whether the Ministry plans for dissemination of information regarding the scheme through 
the Kisan Kendras; and 
 
(d) if so, the details thereof? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ  
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a)  Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) is implementing Central Sector Scheme SVAMITVA with 
the aim to provide the ‘Record of Rights’ to village household owners possessing houses in 
inhabited areas in villages. Legal ownership rights (Property cards/Title deeds) are issued by 
mapping of land parcels using drone technology.   It is being implemented with the collaborative 
efforts of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, State Revenue Department, State Panchayati Raj 
Department and Survey of India (SoI). States need to sign Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) 
with SoI for implementation of  the scheme. So far, 29 States have signed MoU with SoI.  The 
progress made under SVAMITVA scheme is attached at Annexure. 
 
193

(b)  One of the objectives of the scheme is to facilitate monetization of properties of the citi zens 
of rural India by enabling them to use their property as a financial asset by taking loans and other 
financial benefits. Data for grant of property loan through SVAMITVA Scheme is not maintained 
by the Ministry. 
 
(c) and (d)   Funds are sanctioned under Information, Education, Communication (IEC) component 
of the Scheme to States/Union Territories for awareness program formulated by them about the 
surveying methodology and benefits of the scheme.  Funds from other related Schemes of the 
Central and State Government must be converged for IEC activities. For such awareness, various 
methods like materials in the form of manuals, flip books, poster, role plays, puppet shows, 
billboards, public announcements in the villages, information walls, showcasing goo d practices 
through short films, sensitization and mobilization through Gram Sabha etc. are used.

FUNDS UNDER RGSA FOR ANDHRA PRADESH 
  
2796 SHRI V. VIJAYASAI REDDY: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:-

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF PANCHAYATI RAJ 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2797 
ANSWERED ON 22.12.2021 
 
MAKING PANCHAYATI RAJ SYSTEM MORE EFFECTIVE 
 
2797 DR. C.M. RAMESH: 
 
Will the Minister of Panchayati Raj be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government, in consultation with State Governments, proposes to suitably 
amend the existing Act to make Panchayati Raj System more strong and effective, the 
details thereof; and 
(b) whether Government proposes to constitute a high powered committee to study the 
existing Panchayati Raj System and suggest how to make the Panchayati Raj System 
more effective and to meet the technology need of rural India, the details thereof and if 
not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) The Panchayati  Raj system of local self government was introduced by the 73rd 
Amendment of the Constitution of India. Part IX was inserted in the Constitution as a sequel 
to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment in 1993, bestowing the Constitutional mandatory status 
to the ‘Panchayats’. The Government has no proposal under consideration to bring about 
changes in the existing Panchayati Raj system.  
 
(b) Panchayat, being “Local Government”, is a State subject and part of State list of Seventh 
Schedule of Constitution of India. Mandate for setting up of Panchayats is provided by Article 
243 in Part IX of the Constitution of India. Accordingly, the Panchayats are setup and operate 
through the respective State Panchayati Raj Acts. Currently, there is no proposal in the Ministry 
of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) to form any committee to review the functioning of Panchayati Raj 
Institutions (PRIs). To strengthen functioning of PRIs across the country, MoPR has launched 
eGramSwaraj (https://egramswaraj.gov.in), a user friendly web -based portal, which aims to 
bring in better transparency in the decentralised planning, progress reporting, financial 
management, work-based accounting and details of assets created. Further, for ensuring timely 
audit of Panchayat accounts i.e. receipts and expenditu res of Gram Panchayats, MoPR has 
rolled out an online application – AuditOnline (https://auditonline.gov.in). This application not 
only facilitates the auditing of Panchayat accounts but also provides for maintaining of audit 
records. This application stre amlines the process for audit inquiries, draft local audit reports, 
draft audit  paras etc. and thus ensures proper maintenance of accounts by Panchayats to 
improve transparency and accountability.

UNIFORMITY OF LAWS UNDER SVAMITVA SCHEME 
  
2799. SHRI AYODHYA RAMI REDDY ALLA: 
  
Will the Minister of PANCHAYATI RAJ be pleased to state:

(b) whether grievance redressal mechanism is formulated by the Ministry to deal with property 
disputes; and

ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ  
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a)  Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) is implementing Central Sector Scheme SVAMITVA with 
the aim to provide the ‘Record of Rights’ to village household owners possessing houses in 
inhabited areas in villages. Legal ownership rights (Property cards/Title deeds) are issued by the 
State/Union Territory after mapping of land parcels using drone techno logy. It is being 
implemented with the collaborative efforts of the Ministry of Panchayati Raj, State Revenue 
Department, State Panchayati Raj Department and Survey of India (SoI). States need to sign 
Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with SoI for implemen tation of the scheme. So far, 29 
States have signed MoU with SoI. 
 
Land and Land Records is state subject. States/UTs incorporate appropriate provisions in their 
respective Land Revenue Act/Rules/Codes and/or any other administrative document for 
implementation of SVAMITVA scheme and issue of Property Cards. Hence, Ministry has not 
undertaken any initiative for uniformity of State Revenue Laws. The Ministry has, however, 
201

advised the States for the inclusion of certain information like encumbrances, spouse n ame and 
geotags in the Property Card which enhances its value for social and economic advancement. 
 
(b) Distribution of Property Cards/legal ownership rights under SVAMITVA scheme is the 
responsibility of concerned State/UT Government. Respective States/UT s make suitable 
provisions for handling post survey objections/disputes/grievances like correction in name, 
property boundaries, joint holding etc. 
 
(c) The status of survey and Property Cards distribution under SVAMITVA scheme is attached as 
Annexure.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2800 
ANSWERED ON 22.12.2021 
 
ASSESSMENT OF PRIS  
 
2800. SHRI IRANNA KADADI:  
 
Will the Minister of Panchayati Raj be pleased to state: 
 
(a) the key role of panchayats in rural governance and socio-economic development of the 
country; 
(b) whether Government has reviewed/assessed the performance of the Panchayati Raj 
Institutions (PRIs) in the country; 
(c) if so, the details and the outcome thereof including the various loopholes or deficiencies 
noticed in the functioning of panchayats as institutions of local self-government; and 
(d) the details of the grant allocated to Karnataka for PRIs during the last five years? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF STATE FOR PANCHAYATI RAJ 
 
(SHRI KAPIL MORESHWAR PATIL) 
 
(a) In acknowledgment of the key role of Panchayats in rural governance and socio -
economic development of the country, the Panchayati Raj system of local self-government was 
introduced by the 73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India. Part IX was inserted in the 
Constitution as a sequel to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment in 1993, bestowing the 
Constitutional mandatory status to the ‘Panchayats’. Panchayats, being “Local Government”, 
is a State subject and part of the State list of Seventh Schedule of Constitution of India. Mandate 
for setting up of Panchayats is provided by Article 243 in Part IX of the Constitution of India. 
Accordingly the Panchayats are setup and operate through the respective State Panchayati Raj 
Acts. Article 243G of the Constitution envisages Panchayats as institutions of self-government. 
In this regard, this article  provides for devolution, by the State Legislature, of powers and 
responsibilities upon the Panchayats with respect to the preparation of  plans for economic 
development and social justice and for the implementation of schemes for economic 
development and social justice.  The State Legislat ures are to consider the 29 subjects 
illustratively set out in the Eleventh Schedule for devolution to the Panchayats.  Article 243H 
of the Constitution provides for finance for the Panchayats by securing authorization from State 
Legislatures for grants -in-aid to the Panchayats from the Consolidated Fund of the State, as 
also assignment to collect and appropriate , by the Panchayats of the revenues of designated 
204

taxes, duties, tolls and fees. Article 243 -I of the Constitution provides for setting up of a 
Finance Commission every 5 years to review the financial position of Panchayats and make 
appropriate recommendation to improve the financial position of Panchayats. 
 
(b) and (c) The implementation of the provisions of Part IX of the Constitution is reviewed by 
the Ministry of Panchayati Raj (MoPR) from time to time through studies and discussions in 
review meetings with the States. The performance of the Panchayats depends on the extent of 
powers and resources devolved to them, which varies from State to State. The performance of 
Panchayats is monitored by the State Governments. MoPR supports States in building 
capacities of Panchayats for rural governance. It also helps States in developing guidelines for 
participatory planning by Panchayats and preparation of Gram Panchayat Development Plans; 
bringing in efficiency, transparency and accountability for achieving development objectives. 
Further, with a vision to digitalize Panchayati Raj Institutions (PRIs) for empowering rural 
India, Ministry has developed a si mplified work based accounting application –eGramSwaraj 
(egramswaraj.gov.in) to address various aspects of Panchayat functioning including planning, 
budgeting, implementation, accounting and monitoring to make them more transparent, 
accountable and effective as organs of decentralized self-governing institutions. 
 
(d) The details of grants allocated/released to the State of Karnataka under Fourteenth 
Finance Commission, Fifteenth Finance Commission, Capacity Building -Panchayat 
Sashaktikaran Abhiyan (CB -PSA) and Rashtriya Gram Swaraj Abhiyan ( RGSA) during the 
last five years (2016-17, 2017-18, 2018-19, 2019-20 & 2020-21) are given as under: 
              
The details of Grants allocated under Fourteenth and Fifteenth Finance Commission are 
as under:-

are available on [www.powermin.nic.in]. These guidelines have been revised on 01.10.2019.

   GOVERNMENT OF INDIA

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-2804 
ANSWERED ON- 22/12/2021 
ENGAGEMENT OF PRIVATE COMPANIES FOR REPAIR OF NHS 
2804   SHRI K.R.N. RAJESHKUMAR: 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
 
(a) whether Government/NHAI engages private companies for maintenance and repair 
work of the National Highways (NHs);  
(b)    if so, the details and the objectives thereof along with the criteria laid down for engaging 
these private companies;  
(c)     whether Government has reviewed the functioning of these private companies and if so, 
the details and the outcome thereof; and  
(d) the steps being taken to ensure that the work entrusted to these companies is 
completed in the given time frame? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) & (b) Yes Sir, the implementing agencies of MoRTH including NHAI engage private 
companies for maintenance & repair of National Highways. There are basically three methods 
of carrying out maintenance & repair works on National Highways. In the first method, 
contractor is paid for the quantities of repair works undertaken by it at the contract rates. The 
second method is performance based maintenance. In a performance based maintenance 
contract or during defects liability period cum maintenance period of EPC con tract, the 
contractor maintains the road as per the performance standards laid down in the contract and 
lump sum payment is made to the contractor on periodic basis. The third method is performance 
based maintenance during operation and maintenance period of public private partnership 
mode of contract by the concessionaire. In public private partnership as well in EPC contract, 
contractor/concessionaire maintains the project highway during construction period. 
  
(c) & (d) Continuous supervision and monitoring of the maintenance and repair works are 
under taken by Independent Engineer/Authority’s Engineer/ Construction Supervision 
Consultant and officers of the concerned implementing agency of the Government as per 
provisions of respective contract an d guidelines of MoRTH/NHAI to complete maintenance 
and repair works in time/ ensure that performance standards are adhered to throughout the 
maintenance period.

REASONS FOR ROAD ACCIDENTS 
 
2813.  SHRI HARNATH SINGH YADAV:  
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state :- 
(a)  whether there has been any decrease in the number of persons who died and got injured in 
road accidents during the last three years; 
(b)  if so, the State-wise details thereof including Uttar Pradesh; 
(c)  whether it is also a fact that most of the road accidents  occur due to driving for more than 
the permissible number of hours and driving under the influence of alcohol; and 
(d)  if so, the details of action plan of Government to bring down the number of road accidents? 
 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) & (b)           As per the information available with the Ministry, the total number of road 
accidents, persons killed and injured in the country during the last three calendar years 2018 to 2020 
is shown in the table given below :-  
  
Year Total 
Number of

State-wise details thereof including Uttar Pradesh, the total number of road accidents and persons 
killed and injured in the country during the last three calendar years 2018 to 2020 are given in 
Annexure-I. 
  
(c)        The major causes of accidents on the National Highways (NHs) are vehicle condition, road 
engineering, over-speeding, drunken driving/ consumption of alcohol & drug, driving on wrong 
side, jumping red light, Use of mobile phone, etc. 
  
(d)       The Ministry ha s formulated a multi -pronged strategy to address the issue of road safety 
based on Education, Engineering (both of roads and vehicles), Enforcement and Emergency Care. 
Accordingly, various initiatives have been taken by the Ministry as detailed below :- 
  
i. Education:  
a. The Ministry implements a scheme for undertaking publicity measures and awareness 
campaigns on road safety to create awareness among road users through the electronic 
media, print media, NGOs etc. 
b. Observance of National Road Safety Month/Week e very year for spreading awareness and 
strengthening road safety. 
219

c. A Certification Course for Road Safety  Auditors has been commenced in Indian Academy 
of Highway Engineers (IAHE). 
d. Education of general public on traffic rules and their applicability. 
ii. Engineering (both of Roads and vehicles) 
• Road engineering: 
a. High priority to identification  and rectification of black spots (accident prone spots) on 
national highways. 
b. Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning stage. 
c. Ministry has dele gated powers to Regional Officers of MORTH for technical approval to 
the detailed estimates for rectification of identified Road Accident black spots. 
d. Guidelines for pedestrian facilities on National Highways for persons with disabilities have 
also been issued to all States / UTs.  
• Vehicle engineering: 
a. Safety standards for automobiles have been improved in respect of Airbags, Anti -Breaking 
System (ABS), Tyres, Crash test, Whole Vehicle Safety Conformity of Production 
(WVSCoP). 
b. Ministry has notified fitment of Speed Limiting devices on all transport vehicles. 
c. Scheme for setting up one model Inspection & Certification Centre in each State/UT with 
Central assistance for testing the fitness of vehicles through an automated system. 
iii. Enforcement 
a. The recently passed motor vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for strict enforcement 
through use of technology and further provides for strict penalties for ensuring strict 
compliance and enhancing deterrence for violation of traffic rules. 
b. Issue of Guidelines fo r protection of Good Samaritans and draft rules as per MV 
(Amendment) Act, 2019 has been published. 
iv. Emergency care: 
a. The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for a scheme for the cashless 
treatment of victims of the accident during the golden hour. 
b. The National Highways Authority of India has made provisions for ambulances at all 
toll plazas on the completed corridor of National Highways.   
c. Further, 297 ambulances have been upgraded to Basic Life Support as per AIS -125 and 
upgradation for the remaining is under process.

b. Observance of National Road Safety Month/Week every year for spreading awareness and 
strengthening road safety. 
c. A Certification Course for Road Safety  Auditors has been commenced in Indian Academy 
of Highway Engineers (IAHE). 
d. Education of general public on traffic rules and their applicability. 
225

ii. Engineering (both of Roads and vehicles) 
• Road engineering: 
a. High priority to identification  and rectification of black spots (accident prone spots) on 
national highways. 
b. Road safety has been made an integral part of road design at planning stage. 
c. Ministry has delegated powers to Regional Officers of MORTH for technical approval to 
the detailed estimates for rectification of identified Road Accident black spots. 
d. Guidelines for pedestrian facilities on National Highways for persons with disabilities have 
also been issued to all States / UTs.  
• Vehicle engineering: 
a. Safety standards for automobiles have been improved in respect of Airbags, Anti -Breaking 
System (ABS), Tyres, Crash test, Whole Vehicle Safety Conformity of Production 
(WVSCoP). 
b. Ministry has notified fitment of Speed Limiting devices on all transport vehicles. 
c. Scheme for setting up one model Inspection & Certification Centre in each State/UT with 
Central assistance for testing the fitness of vehicles through an automated system. 
iii. Enforcement 
a. The recently passed motor vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for strict 
enforcement through use of technology and further provides for strict penalties for 
ensuring strict compliance and enhancing deterrence for violation of traffic rules. 
b. Issue of Guidelines for protection of Good Samaritans and draft rules as per MV 
(Amendment) Act, 2019 has been published. 
iv. Emergency care: 
a. The Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Act, 2019 provides for a scheme for the cashless 
treatment of victims of the accident during the golden hour. 
b. The National Highways Authority of India has made provisions for ambulances at all 
toll plazas on the completed corridor of National Highways. 
c.   Further, 297 ambulances have been upgraded to Basic Life Support as per AIS -125 and 
upgradation for the remaining is under process 
  
(d)       Ministry has issued guidelines dated 09th November, 2020 for improving the road safety 
through road safety audit at all stage (design stage, construction stage and O&M stage) by 
engaging independent Road safety expert. According to the information available with the 
Ministry, 5803 black spots were identified on National Highways during the period from years 
2016-2018. The total number of black spots in Tamil Nadu is 748.       
  
(e)        No specific fund is allocated to the States/UTs for road safety. But, the States/UTs are 
financially supported by this Ministry for conducting various road safety related activities like 
creating awareness and giving publicity on road safety measures, set ting up various Driving 
Training Centres/Institutes, promoting Good Samaritan Scheme, etc.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
RAJYA SABHA 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO - 2817 
ANSWERED ON-22/12/2021 
STATUS OF IMPLEMENTATION OF VEHICLE SCRAPPAGE POLICY  
2817. SHRI VINAY DINU TENDULKAR: 
 
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:- 
 
(a) whether Government has implemented the Vehicle Scrappage Policy framed for 10 year old diesel 
vehicles and 15 year old petrol vehicles in the entire country; 
 
(b) the parts of the country where this policy is being adhered to and whether any central monitoring centre 
has been formed for this; and 
 
(c) the States in which this policy has been implemented in a uniform manner, if so, the details thereof and 
if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS  
 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
(a) The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways has formulated the Vehicle Scrapping Policy that 
includes a system of incentives/dis -incentives for creation of an ecosystem to phase o ut older, unfit 
polluting vehicles. The policy is based on the criterion of fitness of the vehicle.  In order to enforce 
provisions of the policy, rules have been issued/amended under the framework of the Motor Vehicles Act, 
1988 and Central Motor Vehicles  Rules, 1989. The following final notifications have been issued and 
uploaded on the Ministry's website:-  
(i) GSR Notification 653 (E) dated 23.09.2021 provides the Motor Vehicles (Registration and Functions 
of Vehicle Scrapping Facility) Rules, 2021 for establishment of Registered Vehicles Scrapping Facility 
(RVSF). The notification has come into force with effect from 25th September, 2021. 
(ii) GSR Notification 652 (E) dated 23.09.2021 provides for recognition, regulation and control of 
Automated Testing Stations. The notification has come into force with effect from 25th September, 2021. 
(iii) GSR Notification 714 (E) dated 04.10.2021 provides for upward revision of registration fee, fitness 
testing fee and fitness certification fee of vehicles. The notification shall come into force with effect from 
1st April, 2022. 
(iv) GSR Notification 720 (E) dated 05.10.2021 provides for concession in the motor vehicle tax for the 
vehicle registered against submission of "Certificate of Deposit". The notification sha ll come into force 
with effect from 1st April, 2022.  
(b) and (c) As a part of Vehicle Scrapping Policy, notifications have been issued under the Motor Vehicles 
Act, 1988 and are applicable to all States/UTs. Rules made under Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 are e nforced 
by the respective States/UTs.

system of incentives/dis-incentives for creation of an ecosystem to phase out older, unfit polluting vehicles. The

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO-2819

ALL INDIA REGISTRATION OF VEHICLES 
 
2819.     SHRI SANJAY SETH: 
  
Will the Minister of ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state:- 
  
(a) whether Government has announced a new all-India registration facility for vehicles;  
(b)  the salient features of this registration; 
(c)  the type of vehicles which are eligible for registration under this; and 
(d)  the manner in which this will be helpful to relieve the pain of re-registration of vehicles? 
ANSWER 
  
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
  
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI) 
  
(a) to (d) Ministry of Road Transport & Highways vide G.S.R 594 (E), dated 26.08.2021 has 
introduced a new registration mark for new vehicles  i.e. “Bharat series (BH -series)”. A 
personal vehicle bearing this registration mark shall not require a ssignment of a new 
registration mark when the owner of the vehicle shifts from one State to another. This vehicle 
registration facility under “Bharat series (BH -series)” will be available on voluntary basis to 
Defence personnel, employees of Central Govern ment/ State Governments/ Central/ State 
Public Sector Undertakings and private sector companies/organizations, which have their 
offices in four or more States/Union territories. This will facilitate free movement of personal 
vehicles across States/UTs of India upon relocation. 
 
The motor vehicle tax will be levied for two years or in multiple of two.   After completion of 
the fourteenth year, the motor vehicle tax shall be levied annually which shall be half of the 
amount that was being charged earlier for that vehicle.

c. whether Government is aware that the existing procedure for such access permission is 
cumbersome and lengthy; and 
d. whether Government has any proposal to simplify its procedures and also to delegate 
the powers to grant such permission to lower level with Standard Operating Procedure? 
  
ANSWER 
THE MINISTER OF ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI NITIN JAIRAM GADKARI)

road safety, seamless flow of traffic and so as to avoid any toll leakage/ pilferage.  The 
simplified formats for assessing the technical suitability of the land parcel along with

applications for grant of access permission submitted through online portal.

LACK OF FUNDS FOR MGNREGA 
 
2823  SHRI SANJAY SINGH: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether it is a fact that the flagship scheme of Government, Mahatma Gandhi National 
Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA) scheme has ran out of funds halfway 
through the financial year, in October 2021; 
(b)  if 
so, details thereof and the reasons therefor; 
(c)  whether it is a fact that there are large unpaid wages to workers under the scheme; and 
(d)  the steps taken to ensure that rural workers under the scheme do not experience 
forced labour or delayed wages till new budgetary allocation? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (d): Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme (Mahatma Gandhi 
NREGS) is a demand driven wage employment programme and funds are released to the 
States/UTs on the basis of “agreed to” Labour Budget (LB) and performance of the States/UTs 
during the financial year. The funds allocation has increased more than 18% in the current 
financial year 2021-22 from previous financial year 2020-21 at Budget Estimate (BE) stage from 
Rs. 61,500 crore to Rs. 73,000 crore. Recently, additional fund of Rs. 10,000 crore has been 
allocated for Mahatma Gandhi NREGS as an interim measure.  
 
 
  Fund release to the States/UTs is a continuous process and Central Government is committed in 
making funds available keeping in view the demand for work on the ground.The available funds 
are sufficient to meet the current wage liability. Further, higher allocations may be made upon 
assessment of demand during the Revised Estimate (RE) stage

under- 
 Increase in income by 19% over the base amount.

 Increase in savings by 28% 
 Improved labour force participation of females secondary occupation.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2826 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22/12/2021 
 
 
PROPOSAL FOR MAINTENANCE AND MODERNISATION OF RURAL ROADS 
 
2826  SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:  
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a)  whether any proposal from Governments of Andhra Pradesh, Gujarat and Jharkhand 
regarding maintenance and modernisation of roads in the rural areas is pending with 
Government; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether Government is considering the aforesaid proposals; 
(d)  if so, the details along with the status thereof; and 
(e)  if not, the reasons therefor? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (e) As per the programme guidelines of Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), 
maintenance of roads constructed under the PMGSY is the responsibility of the State Governments 
and all road works are covered by initial five year maintenance contracts to be entered into along 
with the construction contract, with the same contractor, as per the Standard Bidding Document. 
Maintenance funds to service the contract are required to be budgeted by the State Governments and 
placed at the disposal of the State Rural Roads Development Agencies (SRRDAs) in a separate 
maintenance account. On expiry of the 5 year post construction maintenance, PMGSY roads are 
required to be placed under Zonal maintenance contracts consisting of 5 year maintenance including 
renewal as per maintenance cycle, from time to time, which are also financed by the state 
governments.  
The Government of India in the year 2019 launched phase-III of PMGSY for consolidation of 
1,25,000 Km Through Routes and Major Rural Links connecting habitations, inter-alia, to 
Gramin Agricultural Markets, Higher Secondary Schools and Hospitals. The State of Andhra 
Pradesh has been allocated target length of 3,285 Km, against which the State has already been 
sanctioned 2,314 Km road length. The State has recently submitted proposal for the balance 
length. 
The State of Gujarat has already been sanctioned its entire allocated target of 3,015 Km under 
PMGSY-III. 
The State of Jharkhand has been allocated target length of 4,125 Km under PMGSY-III, against 
whi
ch the State has already been sanctioned 979 Km road length. No other proposal of State 
under PMGSY-III is presently pending with the Ministry. 
The implementation period of PMGSY-III is upto March, 2025.

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2827 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22/12/2021 
 
ROAD CONNECTIVITY FOR FARMERS UNDER PMGSY 
 
2827  SHRI SAMBHAJI CHHATRAPATI:  
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) also contains provision for 
repairs and maintenance of roads laid under the scheme since most of those laid in the 
beginning are in very poor condition; 
(b)  if 
so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether the roads connecting the fields could also be made fair-weathered under the 
scheme for easy movement of tractors and other farming equipment; and 
(d)  if so, the details thereof and also the funds allocated under the scheme during 2021-22, 
State-wise? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (b)  „Rural roads‟ is a state subject and maintenance of rural roads is the responsibility of 
the concerned State Governments. 
 However, under various interventions/ verticals of Pradhan 
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY), provisions have been made to ensure/facilitate routine 
maintenance of roads constructed under PMGSY.  
 
 
As per the programme guidelines of PMGSY I, II and RCPLWEA following are the provisions 
with respect to maintenance:- 
 
 
“A separate maintenance component to be funded by the State Government o ut of its resources 
will be provided in the DPR as follows: 
  
i. In case of link routes (new construction) the component shall comprise of 5-year routine 
maintenance. 
ii. In case of associated rural Through Routes not requiring upgradation, the component 
shall include 5-year routine maintenance including one renewal as per cycle. 
iii. In case of Through Routes taken up for upgradation, 5-year routine maintenance and a 
renewal at the end of the period.  
iv. In respect of Hill roads, if construction is in two stages, the initial 5-year maintenance 
contracting will be done at the time of contracting the work for the 2nd 
stage.  Interim 
maintenance, clearance of slips etc., in the period between the 1st and 2nd stage may be 
done departmentally.  
243

 
v. The maintenance component will be contracted out along with the new construction/ 
upgradation, to the same contractor”.  
In respect of roads to be constructed under PMGSY III, the provisions are as under:- 
  
“The roads in the initial five year guarantee period (Defect Liability Period) and post five year 
guarantee period will be maintained by the States.  Periodic renewal of roads after initial five 
year guarantee period or later as per requirement, based on condition assessment shall also be 
carried out by the States.  The States will enter into a Memorandum of Understanding with the 
Ministry of Rural Development, Government of India before launching of the Scheme in the 
concerned State for providing adequate funds for maintenance of roads constructed/ upgraded 
under PMGSY for initial five years routine maintenance, and for further five year routine 
maintenance including periodic renewal as per requirement”. 
 
 
Besides the above provisions for maintenance to be fully funded by the state governments, some 
of the better performing states are provided financial incentives by the central government based 
on the pre-defined parameters which they use for maintenance of roads constructed under 
PMGSY which have crossed the defect liability period. The details of financial incentive 
released to the States is given at Annexure-I. 
 
(c) to (d) There is no such proposal under consideration for construction of fair-weathered roads 
connecting the fields for easy movement of tractors and other farming equipment as of now 
under PMGSY.

INSPECTION OF ROADS UNDER PMGSY 
 
2828   MS. INDU BALA GOSWAMI: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  whether Government is planning to send the National Rural Infrastructure Development 
Agency for inspection work of the rural roads in Himachal Pradesh; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  whether this agency would inspect the roads constructed under the Pradhan Mantri 
Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) in rural areas; 
(d)  whether Government has recently increased the time limit for completing the ongoing 
projects under the PMGSY; and 
(e)  the number of roads in which construction work is going on under this project in 
Himachal Pradesh till date? 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a) to (c) Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) has a three-tiered Quality Control 
Mechanism for ensuring construction of quality road works and durability of road assets under 
PMGSY. Under the first tier, the Programme Implementation Units (PIUs) are required to ensure 
process control through mandatory tests on material and workmanship at the field laboratory. 
The second tier is a structured independent quality monitoring at the State level through State 
Quality Monitors (SQMs) to ensure that every work is inspected at initial stage, intermediate 
stage and the final stage of construction. Under the third tier, which is at the national level, 
independent National Quality Monitors (NQMs) are deployed by National Rural Infrastructure 
Development Agency (NRIDA) for random inspection of road works to monitor quality and to 
provide guidance of senior professionals to the field functionaries. From April, 2018 to 17 th 
December, 2021, a total of 27,312 inspections were carried out by the NQMs in all over India 
including 873 inspections in the State of Himachal Pradesh. The details of inspections conducted 
by the NQMs in the country and Himachal Pradesh year-wise are as under:- 
 
 Years NQM Inspections 
All India Himachal Pradesh  
2018-19 9,356 239 
2019-20 8,989 299 
2020-21 2,653 192 
2021-22 (as on 17.12.2021) 6,314 143 
Total 27,312 873

RURAL MASON TRAINING IN MAHARASHTRA 
 
2829  DR. VIKAS MAHATME: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of masons enrolled, undergoing training, certified as well as institutes 
providing the training under the rural mason training in the State of Maharashtra for the 
preceding two years, the details thereof; and 
(b)  what 
steps has Government taken to provide skill development and for creating 
awareness of rural mason training? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)     A total of 3,647 numbers of masons have been enrolled, out of which 2,418 have been 
certified and 1,229 are undergoing training in the preceding two years in the State of 
Maharashtra. The institutes providing rural mason training in the State during the preceding two 
years are as follows: 
a) Bhaskar Foundation 
b
) Sushil Bahuudeshiya Shikshan Santhan 
c) Pipal Tree Venture Pvt. Ltd. 
d) Cradle Life Science Pvt. Ltd. 
e) BASIX Academy for building Lifelong Employability Ltd. 
  
(b)    The steps taken by the Government to provide skill development and for creating 
awareness of Rural Mason Training are as follows: 
i. Earmarking of 20% of the administrative fund released to the States/UTs may be 
exclusively utilized towards training and certification of Masons including training on 
appropriate building materials and technologies for green housing construction. 
ii. IEC in the form of social media posts, banner, poster video messages etc. have been 
developed to create awareness on Rural mason Training (RMT).  
iii. Houses of old, infirm, and disabled households are constructed under Rural Mason 
Training on priority.  
iv. Partnered with the Construction Skill Development Council of India (CSDCI) and 
National Skill Development Corporation (NSDC) in the implementation of the RMT 
program.  
v
. States/UTs are being encouraged to take up RMT under Recognition of Prior Learning 
(RPL) mode to impart training to rural masons in a time bound manner.

GOVERNMENT OF INDIA 
MINISTRY OF SOCIAL JUSTICE AND EMPOWERMENT 
DEPARTMENT OF EMPOWERMENT OF PERSONS WITH DISABILITIES  
 
RAJYA SABHA 
 
UNSTARRED QUESTION NO.2832 
TO BE ANSWERED ON: 22.12.2021 
 
PERMANENT DISABILITY CERTIFICATE TO PEOPLE SUFFERING FROM SICKLE CELL DISEASE 
2832. SHRI SAMIR ORAON: 
Will the Minister of Social Justice and Empowermentbe pleased to state: 
(a) whether sickle cell is a chronic/incurable disease, if so, whether Government proposes to give permanent 
disability certificate instead of temporary disability certificate to the people suffering from it; 
 
(b) the number of people suffering from sickle cell in India out of that the and number of people from tribal 
community out of that; 
 
(c) whether Government is contemplating on setting up a ‘Centre of Excellence’ in all the States to provide 
timely and proper treatment to sickle cell patients; and 
 
(d) whether Government is considering any pension scheme for these patients? 
 
ANSWER 
 
MINISTER OF STATE FOR SOCIAL JUSTICE & EMPOWERMENT 
(SUSHRI  PRATIMA BHOUMIK) 
(a):  As per the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (RPwD), Act 2016, sickle cell disease means a 
hemolytic disorder characterised by chronic anemia, painful events, and various complications due to 
associated tissue and organ damage; “haemolytic” refers to the destruction of the red blood cells which 
leads to the release of haemoglobin from within the red blood cells into the blood plasma. The Ministry 
notified guidelines for assessment of various specified disabilities including disability caused due to 
blood disorders such as sickle cell disease on 04.01.2018. It was initially prescribed in these guidelines 
that in case of sickle cell disease, in patients with severe disability with score above 80%, permanent 
certificate could be issued. In other cases it was required to be reviewed periodically with at least one 
year of interval as these diseases are progressive in nature. Review of these guidelines is a continuous 
process. These guidelines were last amended with respect to assessment of disability caused due to 
blood disorders on 03.08.2021 vide which it is now stipulated that the process of evaluation is dynamic 
and to be reviewed periodically at an interval of three years instead of one year as stipulated earlier. 
 
 
252

 
(b):  The Ministry relies on Census 2011 data with respect to persons with disabilities. The last Census 
2011 does not provide data regarding persons with sickle cell disease as this disability was not included 
under the repealed Persons with Disabilities (Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full 
Participation) Act, 1995. The Ministry implements Unique Disability Identity Project (UDID) to create 
a national database of persons with disabilities. As per information available on UDID portal, so far 
13677 certificates of disability have been issued for persons with sickle cell disease. 
Further, Ministry of Tribal Affairs has informed that though several States and organisations have 
conducted surveys on incidence and prevalence of sickle cell disease, there is no repository at State or 
Central level giving the exact number of persons having sickle cell disease. 
(c):  Public health and hospitals being a state subject, the primary responsibility of management of 
patients suffering from sickle cell disease including setting up of specialized centers lies with the 
respective State Governments. The Ministry does not have any proposal to set up Centre of Excellence 
in all the States/UTs. 
(d):   Ministry of Rural Development implements Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme 
under National Social Assistance Programme. Under this scheme, central assistance is provided to all 
States/UTs @ Rs. 300/- per month per person with  severe or multiple disabilities aged 18-79 years and 
belonging to family living below poverty line as per the criteria prescribed by the Government. The 
scheme is applicable to persons with disabilities covered under the repealed Persons with Disabilities 
(Equal Opportunities, Protection of Rights and Full Participation) Act, 1995 and the National Trust Act, 
1999. On reaching the age of 80 years, the beneficiaries are paid enhanced central assistance of Rs. 
500/- per month. The States/UTs also top up on central assistance depending on their economic 
capacity.  The States/UTs have been advised to provide disability pension to all categories of persons 
with benchmark disabilities covered under the RPwD Act, 2016.

STATUS OF PMAY-G IN KARNATAKA 
 
2833  SHRI K.C. RAMAMURTHY:

(a)  whether it is a fact that the Ministry proposed to construct 86,000 houses in Phase –II of 
Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana-Gramin (PMAY-G) in Karnataka; 
(b)  if so, the details thereof; 
(c)  the 
status of targets achieved in Phase-I in Karnataka; 
(d)  whether there are still some houses to be constructed in Phase- I; and 
(e)  if so, by when the construction is likely to be completed? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI)

 86,000 
houses for the year 2019-20 and 1,51,715 houses for the year 2020-21 was allocated to state of 
Karnataka based on the number of available beneficiaries in Permanent Wait List (PWL) of

UNSTARRED QUESTION NO. 2834 
TO BE ANSWERED ON 22/12/2021 
 
PMAY-G STATUS AND IRREGULARITIES 
 
2834  SHRI AYODHYA RAMI REDDY ALLA: 
DR. SASMIT PATRA: 
 
Will the Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
 
(a)  the number of houses that have been constructed under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana 
Gramin(PMAY-G), during the last five years, the details thereof, year-wise and State-
wise; 
(b)  whether 
it is a fact that irregularities have been found in implementation of PMAY-G 
scheme across the country; and 
(c)  if so, the details with regard to irregularities and the steps taken by the Ministry in 
addressing the same? 
 
ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
IRANJAN JYOTI) 
 
(a)  Under Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana- Gramin (PMAY-G), a total of 1.67 crore houses have 
been constructed as on 17.12.2021. The Year-wise and State -wise number of houses constructed 
under PMAY-G during last five years and the current year is given at Annexure-I. 
(b) & (c) As per Framework for Implementation (FFI) of PMAY-G, there is a grievance redressal 
mechanism set up at different levels of administration viz., Gram Panchayat, Block, District and 
the State. An official of the State Government is to be designated at each level to ensure disposal 
of grievances to the satisfaction of the complainant. The official who is designated at each level 
is responsible for disposing off the grievance / complaint within a period of 15 days from the 
date of receipt of the grievance / complaint. There is also a procedure of lodging of complaints 
on the Centralized Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) portal 
(pgportal.gov.in). The complaints received in the Ministry of Rural Development through 
CPGRAMS or otherwise on programme implementation are forwarded to the respective State 
Governments/ Union Territory (Union Territory) Administrations for redressal of the grievance.  
As on 17.12.2021, since 01.04.2016 a total of 1,119 complaints relating to irregularities in 
implementation of PMAY-G have been received in the Ministry of Rural Development on 
CPGRAMS. As the State Govt./UT Administration implement PMAY-G, these complaints have 
been sent to the concerned State Governments/Union Territory (UT) Administrations for taking 
necessary action under intimation to this Ministry. Out of 1,119 complaints, 1,068 have been 
disposed and remaining 51 are pending at the level of various State Governments. The State/UT 
wise details of number of complaints received, disposed and pending are given at Annexure-II.

ANSWER 
MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF RURAL DEVELOPMENT 
(SADHVI N
